AS, AR, MR : no change; MS : prominent v wave (d/t pulmonary HTN)
AS, AR, MR : usually no change in JVP; MS : prominent a wave (d/t pulmonary HTN)
AS, AR, MR : elevated JVP; MS : low JVP
questions.exp: The final note prints AS, AR, MR : usually no change in JVP and MS : prominent a wave (d/t pulmonary HTN). (Book p375)

questions.sec: Lanscisis Sign, y Descent Variations, h Wave and the Closing Valve-Disease Note
questions.q: A CCP patient's JVP trace shows a steep early diastolic plunge after the v wave, and a separate TS patient shows a sluggish one. Which printed pair explains them?
opts: Slow y descent in CCP against rapid y descent in TS
Rapid y descent in both, since both raise RA pressure
Rapid x descent in CCP against slow x descent in TS
Rapid y descent in CCP (Friedreich sign) against slow y descent in TS from impaired RA emptying/RV filling
questions.exp: The variations print rapid y descent with CCP → Friedreich sign and slow y descent with impaired RA emptying & RV filling in TS and RA myxoma. (Book p375)

questions.sec: Lanscisis Sign, y Descent Variations, h Wave and the Closing Valve-Disease Note
questions.q: TRUE or FALSE about the p375 descents and h wave.
opts: False — slow y descent causes are CCP and TR
True — a rapid y descent is printed for TS and RA myxoma
True — the y descent follows RA emptying after AV valve opening and is rapid in CCP (Friedreich sign)
False — the h wave sits just after the v wave in short diastole due to ↑ HR
questions.exp: The y descent is diastolic after AV-valve opening with rapid form in CCP (Friedreich sign) and slow form in TS/RA myxoma; the h wave sits just prior to the a wave in long diastole d/t ↓ HR. (Book p375)

units.title: Right-Heart Window, Its Three Indicators, Why the Right IJV Is Preferred and the Neck-Vessel Figures
units.sec: Right-Heart Window, Its Three Indicators, Why the Right IJV Is Preferred and the Neck-Vessel Figures
units.guide:
JVP is the window to the right heart / natural non-invasive RH catheter measuring RA pressure, indicating RH hemodynamics, venous blood volume and venous tone (p370). The right IJV is preferred: carotid triangle between sternal & clavicular heads of SCM, lateral to carotid and deep to SCM, straight line with RA, less extrinsic compression.
Figure labels: carotid sinus, common carotid artery, internal/external jugular veins, subclavian vein & artery, anterior jugular vein, innominate vein, SVC; path of IJv with SCM heads and clavicle. The EJV is not preferred: valves interfere with measurement, invisible in hypotension (vasoconstriction), multiple fascial planes.

units.title: IJV-versus-Carotid Table, Abdominojugular Reflex and the Two-Scale Measurement of JVP
units.sec: IJV-versus-Carotid Table, Abdominojugular Reflex and the Two-Scale Measurement of JVP
units.guide:
IJV vs carotid: superficial & lateral, better seen than felt, 2 peaks & 2 troughs with descents more obvious than crests, digital compression abolishes it, falls with inspiration, elevates with abdominal compression — against deeper & medial, better felt, single brisker visible upstroke, no compression or respiratory effect (p371).
AJR (old hepatojugular reflex): compress periumbilical region 10 sec; ↑ JVP <1 cm for <10 sec transient = normal, ↑ JVP >3 cm for >10 sec = impending right heart failure; principle = compression ↑ venous return which a faulty/dilated RV cannot receive without raised mean pressure. Measurement: scale 1 at JVP top, scale 2 perpendicular at sternal angle, measure x, patient 45° with neck & trunk in line; sternal angle is 5 cm above RA centre.

units.title: Measurement Inferences, Elevated-JVP Cause Groups, Kussmaul's Sign and Waveform Components
units.sec: Measurement Inferences, Elevated-JVP Cause Groups, Kussmaul's Sign and Waveform Components
units.guide:
Inferences: JVP >3 cm above sternal angle elevated; RA pressure = (5 + JVP height cm) cm H2O with >8 elevated; RV end-diastolic pressure = RA pressure (p372). Pulseless rise = SVC obstruction; overload = renal failure, cirrhosis, excess fluid; ↑ RV pressure & ↓ compliance = PS, pulmonary HTN, RVF/RVH, RV infarction; inflow impedance = TS/atresia, RA myxoma, CCP. Kussmaul's sign = JVP rise with inspiration in CCP, TS, RCM.
Waveform: positive a, c, v with descents x, x', y across diastole–S1–systole–S2–diastole; panel aligns a with P, c with S1, x in systole and v after S2.

units.title: a Wave Mechanism and Position, Large a Waves, Cannon and Absent a Waves and the c Wave
units.sec: a Wave Mechanism and Position, Large a Waves, Cannon and Absent a Waves and the c Wave
units.guide:
a wave = RA contraction in diastole just before S1, preceding the carotid upstroke and following the P wave (p373). Large a wave = atria contracting against resistance (RV hypertrophy, RCM, TS, RA myxoma, pulmonary hypertension); giant/cannon a wave = atria against closed TV (regular AVNRT/AVRT; irregular VT with AV dissociation, CHB); absent a wave = AF and hyperkalemia.
c wave = upward bulge of TV during isovolumetric contraction, coinciding with S1; figure captions are large a wave and cannon waves.

units.title: x and x' Descents with Their Variations and the v Wave with Prominent and Reduced Causes
units.sec: x and x' Descents with Their Variations and the v Wave with Prominent and Reduced Causes
units.guide:
x descent = atrial relaxation (position line diastole) while x' = pulmonary valve opening pulling TV down → ↑ RA volume → ↓ RA pressure in systole; prominent x in CCP/CT, reduced/absent in RVF/TR/AF; figure stacks normal, tamponade and constrictive pericarditis (p374).
v wave = atrial filling, mostly systolic with S2 just before its peak; prominent v from ↑ RA volume in ventricular systole (TR, cor pulmonale, RCM, ASD + MR → high venacava pressure d/t RVF); reduced v in hypovolemia/hypotension; photo JVP in TR.

units.title: Lanscisis Sign, y Descent Variations, h Wave and the Closing Valve-Disease Note
units.sec: Lanscisis Sign, y Descent Variations, h Wave and the Closing Valve-Disease Note
units.guide:
Lanscisis sign (as printed) = giant v wave in TR with severe/mild/normal traces (p375). y descent = RA emptying → ↓ RA pressure in diastole after AV-valve opening; rapid y in CCP (Friedreich sign) and causes of prominent v wave; slow y with impaired RA emptying/RV filling in TS and RA myxoma; trace captioned rapid y descent with I, II, K marks.
h wave sits just prior to the a wave in long diastole d/t ↓ HR. Closing note: AS, AR, MR usually no change in JVP; MS prominent a wave d/t pulmonary HTN.
